population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: of the 27.9 pts on in 2032, 55% stayed on (15.35); 12.55 stopped and joined the 9.1 already off (pool 21.65); 50% of the pool restarted (10.8); 15.35 + 10.8 + 3.75 new starters still on = 29.9 on; 21.65 − 10.8 + 1.05 new starters already off = 11.9 off; ever = 37.0 + 4.8 new = 41.8; cycled = 13.4 prior + ~6.0 first-time restarters + ~0.3 among new starters = 19.7 of 41.8 = 47%. Persistence (55%, down from 60%) and restart rate (50%, down from 57%) both fell because of the 2033 price step-up, the tirzepatide shortage and employer coverage dropping from 63% to 47%. Many people who were cut off restarted through cash, Mexico or the gray market rather than going without. Of ~271M adults, current users ≈ 81.0M. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23: 3.4 + 10.89 + 11.04 + 4.6 = 29.9. The 65+ band rose to 20% (~12.5M), carried by the dementia label and Bridge renewal. Income thirds average (37 + 29.5 + 23.2)/3 = 29.9. The middle third was hit hardest by employer retreat but held its share by shifting to cash and gray supply. The bottom third's gain is almost entirely gray and HRSA. Off-drug: 11.9% ≈ 32.2M adults have used and are now off, the largest such pool yet, many of them people who lost employer coverage in 2033–34. Never-used: 58.2% ≈ 157.7M, made up of refusers, contraindicated people, the uninsured in non-expansion states, and a growing group of 18–29s who cannot afford $329–379 and fear counterfeits. Pediatric: 0.95% of ~73M ≈ 690k, of whom ~80k are aged 6–11, down from 880k/150k after the 2033 pediatric label restriction and specialist-only state laws. Children who grew up at drug-household tables are now entering high school.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed Dec 2033 through 2036. Payment rises from $225 to $259/month under the repriced Strategic Supply Agreement, with the $50 copay unchanged. Conditions are kept: ≥5% loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC, and DEXA plus a resistance-training referral for 65+. The tirzepatide-bimagrumab combination is excluded. Bridge obesity users ≈3.9M: 3.9M × $259 × 12 ≈ $12.1B/yr. Medicare overall pays 15.6% of incretin fills ≈ 12.6M users. Medicaid pays 11.5% ≈ 9.3M at $259: 9.3M × $259 × 12 ≈ $28.9B/yr combined. The same seven adherence-waiver states remain. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program FY2034 $4.25B, still unconditional: 2.0M generic liraglutide × $82 × 12 = $1.97B, plus 1.0M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $189 × 12 = $2.27B, = $4.24B, ≈3.0M users (cut from $5.0B/3.6M). TRICARE/VA/DoD ≈2.5M, including ~150k in the Metabolic Readiness Program: 150k × $169 × 12 ≈ $304M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide and ~20 tirzepatide brands at $6–35/month. Mexico (COFEPRIS-approved generic semaglutide, ~$55–80/month in border pharmacies), Canada, Brazil, Turkey and most of Asia sell generics. Chinese originator triple agonists are exported across Latin America. US generic semaglutide ANDAs hold settlement-dated entry rights from 2033, but final approval is stalled by FDA import alerts on their Indian API suppliers. Tirzepatide is protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~81.0M users: commercial 29.6% (24.0M, down from 28.8M and increasingly diabetes/cardiac-coded), Medicare 15.6% (12.6M), Medicaid 11.5% (9.3M), HRSA 3.7% (3.0M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.1% (2.5M), cash/direct 16.7% (13.5M), gray 19.8% (16.0M), = 100%. Shock up: after the Feb 2033 Virginia API plant warning letter, the SSA was repriced in Jul 2033. Direct prices rose to $329 for semaglutide injection (from $249), $379 for tirzepatide (from $299), $179 for oral starts (from $149) and $549 for retatrutide (from $399, back on allocation). Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. The tirzepatide + bimagrumab infusion bundle lists at $2,450/month and is almost all cash or executive-plan funded (~0.5M users). Generic liraglutide cash is ~$129. Employer retreat: coverage for weight management fell from 63% to 47% of employers after the Sixth Circuit's Aug 2033 ruling against PBM-adherence premium differentials and the price step-up. Most firms that dropped it kept coverage under T2D, CVD, CKD and OSA codes, which drove a surge in coding for apnea and prediabetes-with-CVD. Gray composition ≈ 6.5M compounded (503B tirzepatide legal during the Mar 2033–Feb 2034 shortage, then 503A 'personalised'), 5.0M imported generics (Mexican border, Indian mail), 3.0M research-peptide/online 'reta', and ~1.5M counterfeit branded pens, mostly bought by people who thought they were genuine.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance; on allocation since Mar 2033)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Nov 2033, limited launch)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo, incl. low-dose BED presentation)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, obesity with MASH)
Tirzepatide weekly + bimagrumab (activin type II receptor antibody) IV infusion every 4 weeks, co-packaged regimen (approved Oct 2033)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; restricted Jun 2033 to BMI ≥120% of 95th percentile under specialist care)
reduction in risk of dementia in adults ≥55 with type 2 diabetes or obesity plus established cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, Jun 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'quiet' and 'craving freedom' low-dose Foundayo, sold by telehealth subscriptions after a brief BED screen and openly marketed as calm and focus since the Feb 2034 D.C. Circuit ruling
'brain health' semaglutide for 50–65-year-olds outside the dementia label
gambling, compulsive shopping and cannabis reduction, still unlabelled
GLP-1 plus antiresorptive 'bone cover' in 65+, guideline-endorsed
OSA and prediabetes-with-CVD coding to keep employer coverage after weight-management exclusions
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new indication this step. The muscle-preserving driver is realised through the tirzepatide + bimagrumab BLA (filed Mar 2032), approved Oct 2033 after 19 months. Phase 3 showed ~21% weight loss with ~92% of lost mass as fat versus ~70% on tirzepatide alone. The label describes body-composition results, but functional and fracture outcome data are absent, and FDA required a postmarketing fall-and-fracture trial. Infusion every 4 weeks limits it to ~0.5M users at infusion suites, mostly cash. Amycretin, under review at the start, was approved Nov 2033 for obesity with a limited Novo launch (~0.4M users, $449 direct). MariTide supply expanded to ~1.8M users. Retatrutide went back on allocation after the Feb 2033 Virginia API warning letter; the Texas plant, opened Jan 2034, ended the tirzepatide shortage in Feb 2034. A subcutaneous bimagrumab formulation is in phase 3 and not filed. Incretin market ≈ $190B globally in 2034: US volume +9%, US net price +12–15%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Spikes among gray users who receive mislabelled concentrations and among people restarting at full dose after shortage gaps.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; FDA 'restart titration' communication (2033).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed emptying on drug is established; persistence after stopping is still disputed in the literature. MDL 3094 has grown to ~182,000 filed and tolled claims, among the largest active MDLs in the country, fed by plaintiff advertising, which the incretin broadcast ban does not reach. Novo has opened a $3.8B inventory settlement programme for the gastroparesis track; Lilly has not.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis. Combined Novo and Lilly reserves ≈ $9B in 2034 filings.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with retatrutide 12 mg, faster loss, and counterfeit overdose.

Registries of more than 10M person-years still show low absolute risk and no causal confirmation. The litigation now runs ahead of the science: a separate pancreatitis track in MDL 3094 holds ~48,000 claims, and the first bellwether (Jun 2034) returned a $1.1B verdict, mostly punitive, which is on appeal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; FDA declined to strengthen the warning (Apr 2034), citing registry data.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Pleaded in ~9,000 MDL claims after two small Scandinavian case-control signals. Large cohorts show no excess beyond reverse causation from diabetes. Courts have not yet ruled on Daubert.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change; FDA Sentinel analysis ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still a population problem among the ~12.5M users aged 65+. The bimagrumab combination preserves lean mass in trials, but fewer than 4% of 65+ users can access it. The combination's marketing as 'skinny-frail solved' coincides with a ~12% drop in employer-conditioned gym referrals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; Bridge resistance-training referral retained; combination approved with a postmarketing functional-outcome requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Modelled excess ≈ 12.5M users 65+ × 0.5%/yr baseline × HR excess 0.35 ≈ 22,000 hip fractures a year, still concentrated in women and cyclers. Shortage gaps in 2033 added cycling. The final adolescent bone-accrual study (2033) confirmed a ~0.2 SD lower lumbar-spine z-score after more than 3 years, partly but not wholly explained by weight loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA warning retained. Jun 2033 pediatric labelling restriction for ages 6–11. Antiresorptive co-prescription is standard; there are still no fracture-outcome data for the combination in 75+.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in BED, AUD and 'quiet' subscription users.

~8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at high retatrutide doses, and ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure. The effect is now bought on purpose by ~3.4M 'quiet' subscribers on low doses, among whom complaints of flatness are lower but present (~6%).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide Adverse Reactions section and class precaution retained. The FTC's 'calm/focus' consent orders were vacated by the D.C. Circuit (Feb 2034). FDA has no jurisdiction over telehealth claims that do not come from manufacturers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Driven in 2033–34 by employer coverage loss, the tirzepatide shortage and the retatrutide allocation, as well as conditioning cut-offs. About 32M adults are now off drug.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D insufficiency signals persist and are worst in gray users with no clinical contact.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult follow-up and eleven of adolescent follow-up. The first pubertal-timing analysis (2034) shows no clear shift but is underpowered. Pediatric use is down to ~690k.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Registry continues; 11 states require pediatric endocrinology and in-person care for under-18 weight prescribing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a public-health story. Insulin-filled counterfeit Mounjaro/Zepbound pens in Texas and Florida, a Burkholderia-contaminated 503B tirzepatide lot, and unit-conversion dosing errors with multi-dose vials produced, per CDC, ~1,400 hospitalisations and 46 deaths from May 2033 to Dec 2034. Poison-centre incretin calls are up ~60% on 2032.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Alert Network advisories; FDA import alerts on two Indian API makers; ~140 warning letters; CBP seizures roughly tripled but are overwhelmed; three federal indictments of distributors; no prosecutions of users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
'Brain health' prescribing outside the label continues among 50–64s, now often paid in cash after employer exclusions.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Population limits on label; no enforcement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab combination: muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne, transaminase rise, unknown long-term effects of activin blockade
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Muscle spasm in ~40% early in trials, mostly transient. About 0.5M users with under 18 months of real-world exposure. Effects on tendons, the heart and fertility are unstudied beyond 72 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; postmarketing fall/fracture and cardiac-safety studies required; infusion only.

food_and_beverage.state: With nearly 30% of adults on drug, US packaged-food volume keeps falling ~2% a year. The decline is slower than in 2030–32 because millions cycled off in the shortage and coverage retreat, and snack sales briefly ticked up in Q3 2033 in states with heavy employer drop-offs. Protein and fibre formats keep growing. 'Bone-and-muscle' companion products lost some pull at the premium end, where the bimagrumab combination is marketed as making them unnecessary.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volume falls for a sixth year, but by only ~1.5%. Distillers lobby against the 'craving freedom' subscriptions they blame for losing younger drinkers. State excise forecasts keep their incretin line.

restaurants.state: Value chains keep closing suburban units. Fast casual standardises half plates. Operators note that being 'on' is no longer remarked on: menus print 'pen portions' with no explanation. Sports bars near casinos report lower handle and lower tabs.

apparel.state: Size runs are wide and stable. Brands sell 'cycler' lines with adjustable waists for people moving on and off drug. Fall-safe senior apparel is standard in catalogues.

fitness.state: Bridge referrals keep low-cost gyms and PT chains full of older users, but employer-conditioned referrals dried up when coverage did. Premium studios in Scottsdale and Miami rebranded as 'infusion and strength' lounges around the bimagrumab cycle. Mid-market gym memberships are flat.

insurance.state: Employers retreat from weight-management coverage while diabetes, CVD, OSA and CKD codes absorb the demand. Pharmacy trend is ~+11% on the 2033 price step. PBMs that sold adherence verification are repositioning after the Sixth Circuit ruling. Stop-loss carriers add incretin exclusions, and a two-tier system hardens: coded patients are covered, everyone else pays cash or goes gray.

pharma.state: Revenue still grows on volume and price, but the champion bargain is strained. Lilly's Virginia warning letter, its retatrutide allocation and the DPA covenants shape federal pricing. Novo gains share in semaglutide during the tirzepatide shortage but carries the heavier litigation reserve. Generic semaglutide makers hold settlement entry rights they cannot use. Infusion-suite operators are a new sub-industry.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on is now the default and says almost nothing. Being off needs a reason, and people offer one before they are asked: 'my plan dropped it', 'I'm between pens', 'I'm on a holiday', 'I never did'. The newest marker is the body that is lean and fully muscled with no visible effort, read as an infusion body bought at $2,450 a month.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The tiers are visible in bodies. Top-third Scottsdale and Westchester users get the bimagrumab combination and look trained without training. Middle-third users who lost employer coverage in 2033–34 cycle visibly, with weight going up and down around pay periods and shortages. Bottom-third users rely on HRSA liraglutide or Mexican and Indian generics and hold the 'pen-thin' look. The trainer's term 'pen-thin' has become a class slur.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: In Plano, Texas office parks and the Columbus, Ohio suburbs, normalisation is complete. Catered lunches assume half the room is on, and 'Open Table' suppers survive as a church subculture in Grand Rapids and Tulsa without growing. Families no longer discuss a parent skipping dinner. Teenagers barred by state specialist-only laws are the ones who have to explain why they eat a full plate.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule as a lifestyle detail, like a diet once was. 'Off' now prompts questions on a first date: health, money, or principle? Couples split across tiers, with one partner employer-coded under an apnea diagnosis and the other on Mexican generic, and argue about whether to pool for the cash price.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Hunger has become a private, faintly embarrassing symptom, like a cough at the office. The backlash line 'hunger is how we were made' persists in sermons, but the mainstream frames appetite as noise that responsible adults manage. Tennessee and Idaho keep their appetite-liberty laws, and no new state has joined.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Clinical anhedonia ~8% at high retatrutide doses; ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure. The new fact is demand: 'quiet' subscriptions grew from ~1.3M to ~3.4M after the Feb 2034 D.C. Circuit decision vacated the FTC's calm/focus orders and the Dec 2033 broadcast ban pushed marketing onto podcasts, creators and app stores. About 2.6M of them take low-dose Foundayo after a BED screen and ~0.8M take low-dose semaglutide under AUD or cessation workups. All sit inside the cash and commercial shares. None of these uses carries a label; the claims rest on the BED and AUD trials and the retatrutide anhedonia literature.
interior_life.framing: A feature, sold under brand names like Hush, Stillwater and Clearhead: 'freedom from craving', 'quiet focus', 'the space between want and do'. The same effect is still a complaint, 'the grey', for long-term high-dose users. Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. The backlash still says 'chemical contentment', but fewer people listen.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers that dropped coverage do not market it, but workers buy 'quiet' on their own for remote work, trading desks and exam season. Gig drivers and warehouse pickers in Columbus describe low-dose Foundayo as what gets them through a shift without snacks or phone checks. The military readiness programme still tracks tape and DEXA, not mood.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' nights are routine billing. A strand of 'quiet' minimalist music and long-form streaming is marketed to subscribers. Casino and sportsbook operators cite 'quiet' subscriptions by name in 10-Ks. Comedy has moved from 'the grey' to mocking people who pay for it.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule holidays from 'quiet' as well as from the main drug. Sex therapists describe a new presentation: partners on low-dose 'quiet' report little loss of pleasure but less initiation. Conception holidays remain routine.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The pro-access bloc now argues about price, not principle, and blames the SSA repricing and the counterfeit deaths on Washington and India. The backlash coalition won the broadcast ad ban and the pediatric restrictions, then watched marketing move online. Candidates are no longer asked whether they are on; one who said she was off was asked why.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access on approvals (bimagrumab combination, amycretin) but restrictive on the edges: pediatric labelling narrowed, a broadcast advertising ban, state in-person and specialist rules, and import alerts. Enforcement is concentrated on counterfeits and contaminated supply, and it is losing ground.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Bridge renewed through 2036 at $259/$50 with conditions; HRSA $4.25B, unconditional; DoD readiness at a $169 federal price; ACA cessation mandate unchanged. The Bridge renewal act bars participating manufacturers from broadcast and streaming DTC advertising for weight-indication incretins.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Employer conditioning is in retreat after the Sixth Circuit held in Aug 2033 that PBM fill data cannot serve as a wellness 'reasonable alternative standard'. The Fifth Circuit upheld it in Mar 2034, creating a split, and certiorari has been granted for the 2034–35 term. Medicaid waivers and Bridge conditions still run on PDC, which everyone knows is degraded by skip-but-fill. Nine states require an in-person exam before retatrutide ≥8 mg or the bimagrumab combination, and cap fills at 90 days.
state.workforce_or_military: The Metabolic Readiness Program grew to ~150k. DoD and VA kept priority supply through the 2033 tirzepatide shortage while civilians were rationed, a fact the backlash and pro-access populists both use. Religious-accommodation requests reached ~3,400. Police and fire contracts in Phoenix, Houston and Chicago continue. Some smaller departments dropped coverage with their health plans.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The champion model was shaken: one warning letter at Lilly's Virginia plant moved federal prices up. A WTO panel on India's Section 232 complaint was established in 2033, and FDA import alerts on two Indian API makers are read in Delhi as protectionism. Mexican border pharmacies in Nogales, Reynosa and Tijuana run incretin-only storefronts. Chinese originator and counterfeit product enters through Latin American transshipment. Novo still pays duty on Danish API.

events.event: FDA issues a warning letter to Lilly's Virginia API plant over particulate and endotoxin findings. Retatrutide returns to allocation, tirzepatide goes onto the FDA shortage list (lifting 503B compounding limits), and in July the Strategic Supply Agreement is repriced: TrumpRx semaglutide rises to $329, tirzepatide to $379, oral starts to $179 and retatrutide to $549.

A CDC health alert links insulin-filled counterfeit Mounjaro pens in Texas and Florida and a Burkholderia-contaminated 503B tirzepatide lot to a run of hospitalisations. FDA places import alerts on two Indian API makers, which stalls the settlement-dated US generic semaglutide launch. By end-2034 CDC counts ~1,400 hospitalisations and 46 deaths.

The Sixth Circuit rules that PBM adherence data cannot be used as a wellness 'reasonable alternative standard' for premium differentials. Large employers including two auto suppliers and a national retailer drop weight-management coverage and keep only diabetes, cardiac, apnea and kidney codes. Employer coverage falls from 63% to 47% by end-2034.

FDA approves Lilly's tirzepatide plus bimagrumab regimen after a 19-month review. Lilly markets it as 'lose the fat, keep the frame' at $2,450 a month by infusion, and FDA requires a postmarketing fall-and-fracture trial.

Congress renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2036 at $259 a month and bars participating manufacturers from broadcast and streaming advertising of weight-indication incretins. The FDA's June pediatric restriction and 11 states' specialist-only laws limit under-18 use. In Feb 2034 the D.C. Circuit vacates the FTC's 'calm/focus' orders, and telehealth 'quiet' subscriptions advertise freely online.

The first pancreatitis bellwether in MDL 3094 returns a $1.1B verdict against Novo Nordisk, mostly punitive. Filed and tolled claims pass 180,000 across the gastroparesis, pancreatitis and pancreatic-cancer tracks. Novo opens a $3.8B gastroparesis settlement programme, and Lilly declines to join.

open_tensions: The Supreme Court will decide the circuit split on PBM adherence data in 2035. Employers, the seven Medicaid waiver states and the Bridge all rely on PDC figures that skip-but-fill has made unreliable, and a ruling either way would re-sort millions of people between covered and cash.

US generic semaglutide is legally entitled to launch but stalled behind import alerts on the same Indian API supply that feeds the gray market. The India WTO panel, Lilly's plant remediation and the 2033 price step-up all bear on whether the champion bargain survives to the Bridge's 2036 expiry.

The muscle problem is 'solved' at $2,450 a month by infusion for about half a million mostly affluent users. Meanwhile ~12.5M older users on the dementia label rely on referral slips and antiresorptives, ~22,000 excess hip fractures a year continue, and nobody knows what long-term activin blockade does.

The broadcast ad ban and the FTC's court loss have together moved the selling of reward blunting from television to unregulated online channels. The 180,000-claim MDL and the counterfeit deaths keep public trust falling even as being on the drug becomes the unremarkable default.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: Everyone's On It. Now Ask Whose Pen: Price Hikes, Fake Mounjaro, and the $2,450 Infusion That Keeps the Rich Strong
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2034 nobody remarks on it. Eighty-one million American adults are on an incretin drug, almost three in ten, and in the office parks of Plano and the suburbs of Columbus a catered lunch assumes half the table is on. The person who has to explain themselves is the one who is not: the plan dropped it, the pen is late, I'm on a holiday, I never did. People now offer the reason before anyone asks.

The drugs are everywhere, but they cost more than they did two years ago. In February 2033 the FDA found particulates and endotoxin at Lilly's new Virginia ingredient plant, the plant the national-champion bargain was built on. Retatrutide went back on allocation, tirzepatide went onto the shortage list, and by July the federal deal had been repriced upward. The cash portal now sells semaglutide at $329, tirzepatide at $379 and the starter pill at $179. Generic semaglutide was supposed to arrive in 2033 under the patent settlements. Its makers hold the right to launch, but their Indian ingredient suppliers are under FDA import alerts, so it has not.

Employers left at the same time. In August 2033 the Sixth Circuit ruled that pharmacy refill data could not be used to set wellness premiums, because everyone knew people collected refills they did not inject. Large employers stopped covering weight loss and kept paying only for diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea and kidney codes. Coverage fell from sixty-three percent of employers to forty-seven. Physicians found apnea in a lot of patients. Those without a qualifying code pay cash, cross the border at Nogales for Mexican generics at sixty dollars a month, or buy from the gray market, which now supplies about sixteen million people.

That market became a public-health story. Counterfeit Mounjaro pens filled with insulin reached Texas and Florida, a contaminated compounded lot carried Burkholderia into infusion bags, and unit-conversion errors filled poison-centre logs. The CDC counts forty-six deaths and about fourteen hundred hospitalisations. That is not a catastrophe, but it is enough to make a pharmacist in El Paso keep a lot-number lookup open on her screen.

In Washington the response was restriction at the edges. The Bridge renewal kept Medicare paying, now $259 a month with the same weight-loss, adherence and bone-scan conditions. It also banned drug makers from advertising weight drugs on television. The FDA narrowed use in young children after the bone-accrual study, and eleven states now require a pediatric endocrinologist for anyone under eighteen. The advertising moved online. A federal appeals court struck down the FTC's orders against 'calm' marketing, and subscriptions called Hush and Stillwater now sell low-dose pills as freedom from craving and quiet focus to three million adults. Sportsbooks name them in their annual reports.

The muscle problem is now treated as solved for people who can pay for it. Lilly's tirzepatide-and-bimagrumab regimen, approved in October 2033, keeps lean mass while the fat goes, by infusion every four weeks at $2,450 a month. In Scottsdale and Miami, gyms rebranded as infusion lounges. Medicare does not cover it. The twelve and a half million older users who came on for the dementia label still get a resistance-training referral and a bone drug, and the hip fractures, about twenty-two thousand excess a year, continue.

The lawsuits grew alongside the market. More than a hundred and eighty thousand claims sit in the federal gastrointestinal docket, and a Philadelphia jury awarded $1.1 billion over a pancreatitis case the registries cannot confirm. Novo set aside money and Lilly did not. Snack sales fell a little less this year because so many people cycled off. From the outside the country looks lean and calm.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Peña sets her alarm for 4:40 so she can be at the DeConcini crossing before the line builds. The district's letter is still on the fridge under a magnet shaped like a saguaro: Effective July 1, weight management is no longer a covered benefit. Her A1c is 5.9, one tenth too good to qualify.

In Nogales the farmacia has a laminated sign in English, SEMAGLUTIDA GENÉRICA, and a COFEPRIS licence framed beside a Virgin of Guadalupe. Three pens, $186. The girl at the counter tapes the receipt to the box without being asked. On the walk back Marisol photographs the lot numbers anyway and sends them to her sister, who forwards everything about the Houston pens.

The CBP officer asks what she's bringing in. She says medicine, ninety days. He nods. Half the line has the same paper bag.

At payroll she processes a retirement and eats seven almonds. Her supervisor, who is on Zepbound under an apnea code, mentions she's trying Hush, the craving-freedom one: "It's not about weight. It's about getting through spreadsheets."

After work Marisol picks up her mother from the Sun City strength class her Bridge referral pays for. Her mother shows her the bruise from the DEXA bench, laughing.

At dinner her son Teo, fifteen, takes seconds of calabacitas. His friend at the table watches him like he's done something brave.

At nine she sets the Mexican pen on the counter next to the old Lilly one and compares the clicks. Then she injects her thigh.
